text:
Maya: sec-bot alerted on a CI artifact: possible customer API key in release-2026-03-20.tar.gz
sec-bot: scanner rule 'cust-key-pattern-v2' MATCH in build/release/bin/config.json
Maya: snippet (masked): "cust_live_4f3a****f2b" — looks like a live customer key. Starting triage.
Ryan: ACK. First action: revoke if it's customer-managed or issue rotation. Who owns onboarding for that customer?
Alex: Can we confirm which customer? Search for key hash in our usage logs and key registry.
Joni: I'm running a quick grep across S3 -> `/s3/ci-artifacts/2026/03/20/release-2026-03-20.tar.gz` and dumping file list
Joni: found file, extracting config.json now
Joni: extracted. file shows field `client_api_key: "cust_live_4f3a....f2b"`
Maya: tagging CS and Legal. @CS-Sara please hold on pre-notify until we have impact. @Legal FYI for potential disclosure.
CS-Sara: standing by. Need list of affected customers and whether PII was included.
Alex: running usage query: `SELECT count(*) FROM api_logs WHERE api_key_hash = sha256('cust_live_4f3a...f2b') AND ts >= '2026-03-01'` — no hits in last 30 days
Ryan: good sign. Also check credential creation logs and RBAC to see which service could have had access to that key during CI
Maya: RBAC audit: the artifact was produced by pipeline `ci-release-2026` which uses service account `ci-builder@redwood`. That SA has S3 read on `ci-artifacts` only.
Alex: That implies the key was bundled by the repo or build env, not grabbed from secrets store. Check KMS usage logs — was the pipeline able to decrypt any secrets via KMS?
Joni: KMS logs: no decrypt event from `ci-builder` in the 24h window. Looks like plaintext in tree.
Ryan: Containment plan: 1) Create incident ticket INC-1824 2) Rotate/revoke the exposed customer key with urgency 3) Run org-wide scan for similar artifacts 4) Update scanner rules to catch this pattern earlier
Maya: On rotation: which API supports revocation? Customer uses Hosted API. @Alex can you trigger revoke and issue new key via the Customer Keys API? Use `POST /v1/customers/:id/keys/revoke` with reason "leak-detected-ci" then generate new key and mark rotated=true
Alex: doing revoke now. calling `curl -XPOST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/customers/982/keys/revoke -d '{"key_hash":"4f3a...f2b"}'` -> 202 Accepted
Alex: revoke completed. new key generated and delivered to customer contact? Not yet, CS will handle notify and rotation coordination
CS-Sara: I'll prepare a scoped notification. We'll offer immediate rotation assistance and monitoring. Will hold official notice pending Legal
Legal: please draft a short disclosure: what happened, mitigation (revoked key), recommended rotation steps, and what we're doing to prevent reoccurrence. No admission of systemic breach.
Maya: Post-containment actions: - run full CI artifact scan for last 90 days - add pre-merge CI check to reject any commit with `cust_live_` pattern - increase audit log retention for key operations to 180d - make KMS mandatory for repo-managed secrets where possible
Ryan: Also create RBAC follow-up: restrict `ci-builder` to not have direct write access to repo files that can inject keys; rotate all deploy pipeline secrets and enforce secret-manager use
Joni: kicking off job `infra/scans/ci_artifact_leak_sweep` now. ETA 25m
sec-bot: sweep results queued: 12 artifacts matched looser pattern, 3 require manual review
Maya: Great. Assigning manual review to @Alex and @Joni. Please update INC-1824 with findings and timeline
Alex: will update. scheduling postmortem meeting for tomorrow 10:00 PT. Adding action items to the ticket
CS-Sara: once Legal gives go, I'll send customer-facing note and open a support ticket for that customer. Also prepping standard template
Maya: thanks all. keep replies short in thread. We want clear timeline in the ticket. Postmortem doc: /docs/security/incidents/INC-1824
